items.title: TSCO ($$): Nov 13 $37.5 calls bought
items.summary: 6,000 Nov 13 (weekly) $37.5 calls bought on 11/4, rolling up from the $35s, as shares gapped to a 60-day high, 5,000 Nov $34 calls bought 10/19 (stock replacement), and 3,500 Nov $33.5 short puts opened; spot $36.60. Desk sees a rural retail / pet consumables name, down ~27% YTD and below the 200-day since February, but holding above the 8/21-day EMAs and 50-day with a bullish MACD cross. Desk watches a close through the 200-day as the trigger; traffic and pet comps improving.

items.title: UBER ($$): Jan 2029 $80 puts sold
items.summary: 900 Jan 2029 $80 ITM puts sold (~$1.5M) on 11/4 after Q3, 2,750 Jan $52.5 ITM calls bought (~$4M) into earnings 11/3, and large Dec $55 and $57.5 short-put open interest from late October; spot $69.90. Desk sees a mobility + delivery leader, down ~15% YTD; reclaimed the 21-day EMA on 2x volume after Q3, basing off the late-October low with the 50-day as first resistance. Cheap vs its own 10-year FCF range; desk lean is following long-dated put sellers on pullbacks.

items.title: INSM joins the $$$ Shopping List

items.title: Oil's war premium cracks
items.summary: Brent fell 11.4% Monday, its biggest daily drop in six months, after Iran signaled a return to talks. The open question is how much of oil was pricing real supply loss versus insurance, and a gap remains between negotiations and restored Gulf flows.

items.title: BofA: the data-center power squeeze and the elections
items.summary: BofA's utilities team sees state regulators and power-bill affordability, not which party wins, as the bigger election risk for the AI electricity buildout. Texas is the center of demand but its regulatory timetable matters most; Georgia and Ohio show how affordability politics reshape data-center economics.

items.title: Goldman: risk appetite breaks, leverage doesn't
items.summary: October saw one of the largest monthly drops in Goldman's risk appetite gauge in two decades, the sharpest deterioration since November 2021, but not yet at contrarian extremes. Hedge funds cut directional exposure while keeping gross leverage elevated, and the stock-vol-yields relationship is shifting, widening outcomes both ways.

items.title: Goldman: one more crowded long to clear
items.summary: Tech-focused hedge funds lost nearly 12% in October and managers are protecting year-end P&L rather than rebuilding risk. The net-exposure bounce is mostly short covering with gross leverage still very high; semis and AI infrastructure were liquidated while Mag 7 positioning sits near the year's highs and could become a source of funds.

Desk sees a durable 2027 earnings story as merger integration costs roll off, with the Swiss capital rule as the main overhang.

items.title: Goldman: midterms and the policy risks markets may misprice
items.summary: A Democratic House looks increasingly likely but the Senate is less certain than prediction markets imply. Winning seats is not the same as changing policy; bigger fiscal fights likely come in 2027, data-center limits are more likely at state level, and effective tariff rates are expected to rise after the vote.

items.title: Goldman: seven signs from the hedge fund book
items.summary: Hedge-fund net leverage is near levels that historically preceded 20%+ drawdowns while the S&P sits only modestly off the highs. Implied correlation is near the lows, defensives look expensive, and systematic selling is a near-term obstacle.

items.title: Morgan Stanley: hedge funds go underweight AI
items.summary: Hedge funds are underweight AI for the first time since early 2023, the most sustained gross reduction in the prime-book history. Single-stock vol versus the index is at a record and pairwise correlation is under 10%, which may be a final clearing phase.

items.title: Goldman: spec gold futures selling
items.summary: About $19.5B of speculative gold futures were sold over five weeks, about $8B of that from Oct 20–27, mostly smaller reportable and non-reportable traders. About $3,850 is flagged as support.

items.title: BofA: turning constructive on US tech IG bonds
items.summary: Tech investment-grade bonds are at their worst relative underperformance in about 30 years. AI issuers have raised about $182B in bonds and $89B in equity in 2026, and the next big risk-on window is seen in the first half of 2027.

items.title: Bloomberg: equal-weight beat cap-weight by the most since 2009
items.summary: October's equal-weight minus cap-weight S&P gap was the widest since April 2009, while the Nasdaq 100 sat about 9% off its peak.
